items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: one of your friends, I was once in Joe Williams’ dressing room and we were talking... Joe looked at me and said, “you and I are survivors.”

ctx.x: And Joe Williams was, at the time —
Joe Williams was the key figure I thought in the band, except for Basie.

items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember, years later, I was in Joe Williams’s dressing room. We were talking about musicians we’d both known... Joe looked at me and said, “You and I are survivors.”

ctx.x: . . . and then this show where they had Ahmad Jamal – a group by Ahmad Jamal and a group led by Buck Clayton. There’s this wonderful image of Ben Webster, Jo Jones, George Duvivier, Vic Dickenson, all playing – Hank Jones – and you’re there with your beard and your pipe, looking very natty – no pun intended. You’re listening to the music. And how I’m beginning to realize that you and Ben, you and Jo, and you and these people – you weren’t some jazz writer from the magazine who happened to be at the session. You…

I never felt, not being a musician, that I was totally part of the tribe, as it were. But I remember, years later, I was in Joe Williams’s dressing room. We were talking about musicians we’d both known who had come to an untimely end of their own doing, to a large extent. Joe looked at me and said, “You and I are survivors.” I figured, this is like I’d been knighted, that he could consider me in the same class that he was. But I’ll tell you: you mentioned that particular Herridge show, and also Herridge with Gil…
